references.text: Parallel text describing the second row of the same precious stones (carbuncle, sapphire, and diamond) on the breastplate when it was actually made.
Ezekiel describes the king of Tyre as covered with precious stones, including sapphire, which resembles the stones on the high priest's breastplate.
Job mentions sapphire as a valuable gemstone found in the earth, the same stone mentioned in the second row of the breastplate.
Wisdom is compared to precious stones, including sapphire, emphasizing the value of the stones on the high priest's breastplate.
The foundations of the new Jerusalem are adorned with precious stones, including sapphire, linking back to the stones on the breastplate.
Typological fulfillment: The tribes represented in the breastpiece in Exodus foreshadow the foundation stones of the new Jerusalem.
